avatar.description: The account's picture, as in dev.knotless.getProfile#profileView.

bot.description: Whether its knotless profile says it is a bot, as in dev.knotless.defs#actorView.

handle.description: The handle the account claims, when it resolves back to it; else the DID.

changed.description: A pull or an issue moved to another state.

subjectState.description: Where the subject stands now, whoever moved it there.

commented.description: A comment or review on a pull or an issue, or a comment on a gist.

subject.description: The pull or issue, or the gist's own dev.knotless.repo record.

subjectState.description: Where the subject stands now, whoever moved it there.

title.description: The subject's title: for a gist, its description, else its name.

merge.description: Whether the commit has more than one parent. Absent when not.

created.description: A repository or a gist created, or forked from another.

kind.description: gist for a gist, a repository whose record says it is one. Absent for any other repository.

eventView.description: Something an account did to a repository.

createdAt.description: When the record saying so was made.

main.description: What happened on the public repositories an appview has indexed, newest first: repositories created and forked, refs pushed and deleted, pulls and issues opened, discussed and moved between states, and repositories starred. With filter `following`, what the account asking and those it follows did, and anything done on its repositories and those it starred; without, the same for anyone, but no stars. Without `actor`, what a repository's bots said or pushed on it is left out: the runners and triagers its record names, but its owner and collaborators. A pull a runner merged landing the merge queue is shown as merged by whoever queued it. Optional authentication: asked as an account, with a service token or the pages' session cookie, what happened on the private repositories it may read too, its own and those it was proven a member of, as the server's index of their spaces has it, whoever did it, whom it follows or not; and the answer is that account's alone.

cursor.description: Where the next page starts, when there may be one.

actor.description: Only what this account did: the repositories it created, the refs it pushed, the pulls, issues, comments and changes of state it wrote, and the repositories it starred.

cursor.description: Where the page starts: a previous page's cursor.

filter.description: Whose doings: `everyone`'s, or with `following`, those of the account asking and whom it follows, which needs an account to ask.

kind.description: Only what is of this kind: refs pushed and deleted, pulls or issues opened and moved between states, comments, repositories starred, repositories created and forked but gists, or gists created and forked. A kind the appview does not know answers nothing.

opened.description: A pull or an issue opened.

subjectState.description: Where the subject stands now, whoever moved it there.

pushed.description: A ref created or moved, or moved again and again by one account, each move within an hour of the last, as one. A new ref brings what the repository's default branch did not reach just before, nor its fork source's; a fork's copies of its source's refs are not events.

commits.description: The newest of the new ones, newest first.

count.description: Commits the push brought; 100 means at least that many. A forced push's leave out those it brought again: the same author, at the same time, with the same message as a commit it left behind.

forced.description: Whether the ref moved to where it no longer reaches some of what it did, as a rebase or a rewrite does. Absent when not.

new.description: Of those, the commits no other ref of the repository had before, and no event before it on the same page lists; the rest are only counted.

ref.description: The full ref name, such as refs/heads/main.

to.description: The commit the ref was left at, in hex: what the push brought, which a page can link to after the ref is gone.

repoView.description: A repository, under the name it has now.

description: What happened on the public repositories an appview has indexed, and on the private ones the account asking may read, newest first.
